suite: embedded scripting runtimes in a Rust host (in-process), same start/memory/tool-call definitions as the C Lua harness
buildProfile: release, opt-level=3, lto=fat, codegen-units=1, one standalone crate and target dir per engine
sessionDefinition: every engine builds its whole engine per session (nothing shared between sessions: no shared engine, compile context, standard library, or runtime), applies its documented limits, registers the host call function, then evaluates 1 + 1 and reads 2 back in Rust; engines with a large immutable part an embedder could share (rune Context, steel prelude, rhai standard package, roto runtime) would start faster and use less memory per session if shared, which is not measured here
stabilityNote: each entry's stabilityCheck holds the same binary's primary numbers from an earlier full pass on this host minutes before; differences show run-to-run noise on a shared, busy machine
callKind: sync = the guest calls a registered Rust function on its own stack; async = the guest suspends at the call and the host resumes it with the reply (no Rust callback)
phaseOrder: each engine runs in its own process: memory first (one warm-up session dropped, malloc_trim, then K live sessions), then start, then tool calls in one session

units.startUs: median microseconds from creating a fresh session through reading 1 + 1 == 2 in Rust
units.memoryBytesPerSession: RSS growth (/proc/self/statm) per live session after its first response, measured first in a fresh process after malloc_trim
units.toolCallWallUs: median of per-batch mean wall time per call, batches of 1,000 calls, after warm-up
units.toolCallCpuUs: CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID over all measured calls divided by measured calls
units.toolCallWallMeanUs: total measured wall time divided by measured calls (includes GC pauses the median skips)
units.toolCallSlowestBatchUs: per-call mean of the slowest 1,000-call batch

engines.limitsEnabled: Lua::new() (ALL_SAFE libs), sandbox(true), set_interrupt (returns Continue), set_memory_limit(64MiB)
notes: Session = Lua::new() + memory limit + interrupt + global call + sandbox(true); call is registered before sandbox(true) so it sits in the read-only globals.
Host fn is lua.create_function(|lua, Table| -> Table); fields read with Table::get and the reply built with create_table_with_capacity(0, 3), mirroring the C harness's lua_getfield/lua_setfield.
Bundled Luau from luau0-src 0.22.0+luau740.

Secondary measurements in the same session (sandbox kept): after remove_interrupt() toolCallWallUs=1.9980, toolCallCpuUs=2.0303; after also set_memory_limit(0) toolCallWallUs=0.6316, toolCallCpuUs=0.6583 (1,000,000 calls each). With a memory limit set, mlua runs each allocating table operation (create_table, set) as a protected call so an allocation failure cannot unwind through Rust.

Luau allocates GC objects from per-size-class pages, so a fresh mlua Luau state reports about 436 KB from Lua::used_memory(), of which about 182 KB is resident before our call function, limits, and sandbox are added (separate diagnostic, 1,000 states).

engines.limitsEnabled: Runtime::set_memory_limit(64MiB), set_max_stack_size(1MiB), set_interrupt_handler (returns false); Context::full has no I/O modules
notes: Native QuickJS: rquickjs-sys 0.14.0 bundles quickjs-ng 0.16.2 (not Bellard QuickJS), compiled by cc with the crate's default flags; a native comparison point for QuickJS compiled to Wasm.
Session = new Runtime (own GC heap and memory limit) + Context::full + global call; runtimes are not shared across sessions.
Host fn is Function::new(ctx, fn(Ctx, Object) -> Result<Object>); reading args.s copies it into a Rust String to take its length (rquickjs exposes no borrowed length), about 22 bytes per call.

engines.limitsEnabled: max_operations=1000000000, max_call_levels=64, max_expr_depths=64/32, max_string_size=1MiB, max_array_size=100000, max_map_size=10000, max_variables=1000, max_functions=1000, max_modules=0, DummyModuleResolver (Engine::new installs a FileModuleResolver), print/debug discarded
notes: Session = Engine::new() (standard package rebuilt per engine) + limits + registered call + Scope; the engine is not shared across sessions.
Host fn is register_fn("call_tool", fn(Map) -> Result<Map>); the map argument is moved in, reply map keys are inline SmartStrings.
Guest is a script function called once with call_fn(run, start, count).
The host function is named call_tool: `call` is reserved in Rhai for calling function pointers.

engines.limitsEnabled: runtime::budget::with(1000000000 instructions) and alloc::limit::with(64MiB) around every Vm call; Context::with_default_modules (no fs/process/net modules)
notes: Session = Context::with_default_modules() + module with call + RuntimeContext + compiled Unit + Vm; nothing shared across sessions, so start includes building the default-module context and compiling `pub fn main() { 1 + 1 }`.

Host fn is Module::function("call", fn(&Object) -> VmResult<Object>); Rune objects key on heap-allocated rune::alloc::String, so each reply allocates three key strings (the guest's object literals do the same).
Tool-call guest is compiled into a second Unit in the same Context/RuntimeContext and run by its own Vm.

engines.limitsEnabled: KotoSettings::with_execution_limit(600s) (wall-clock deadline checked between instructions); io and os modules removed from the prelude (Koto's default prelude has file I/O and os.command); no memory or instruction-count limit API; `import` can still load .koto files from disk (no setting disables it)
notes: Session = Koto::with_settings (fresh core-library prelude per runtime) minus io/os, plus prelude call.
Host fn is KMap::add_fn("call", |ctx| ...) on the prelude; reply keys reuse preallocated KStrings.
Guest is an exported Koto function invoked with Koto::call_function.

engines.limitsEnabled: none available: Roto has no instruction, time, or memory limit API; it is sandboxed by construction (only registered Rust functions and types are reachable, no I/O in the standard library)
notes: Roto is statically typed and JIT-compiled with Cranelift, so `1 + 1` means compiling `fn main() -> i64 { 1 + 1 }` to machine code: session = Runtime::from_lib(our library) + compile + call.

Roto has no maps, and its records cannot be passed to Rust functions, so the call argument is the closest structure: registered Rust types built by host constructors, call(Call.new(id, "lookup", Args.new("hello from the sandbox"))). That is three native calls per tool call (two constructors plus call); the reply is a registered Reply type read through native accessor methods (reply.id()).
Roto has no exceptions, so the guest counts id mismatches and the host asserts zero.
The tool-call loop is compiled machine code making three direct native calls per iteration, so it measures Roto's FFI and native-call cost rather than an interpreter.

engines.limitsEnabled: Engine::new_sandboxed() (no I/O primitives, dylib loading blocked) with the crate's `sandbox` feature (bounded equality recursion); no instruction or memory limit exists: Engine::with_interrupted stores a flag that the 0.8.3 VM never reads
notes: Session = Engine::new_sandboxed(): deep-clones a per-thread bootstrap kernel image, builds a macro Kernel, then compiles and runs the prelude; plus register_fn(call). The kernel image itself is built once per thread and is excluded by the warm-up session and warm-up runs.
Host fn is register_fn("call", fn(SteelVal) -> Result<SteelVal, String>); call and reply are immutable im-rc hash maps keyed by symbols (preallocated on the host side).
Guest loop is a tail-recursive local function; call_function_by_name_with_args runs it.
memorySessions stopped at the 3 GiB growth budget (252 live sessions); startRuns is the at-least-40 slow-engine count.

engines.limitsEnabled: Evaluator::set_max_callstack_size(100), set_max_heap_size(64MiB, best-effort), set_max_tick_count(1000000000) on every evaluator; Dialect::Standard (no while loops, no recursion); hermetic by design (no I/O builtins)
notes: Session = Globals (standard + our call module) + Module; an Evaluator is created per evaluation and is not kept. Modules only exist inside Module::with_temp_heap, so the memory phase nests sessions by recursion after pre-touching the stack it uses (memoryExtraStackBytes <= 0 means no stack was counted).
Host fn is a #[starlark_module] native fn(Value, Heap) -> Value; reply dict keys are static frozen strings.

starlark-rust only collects garbage between top-level module statements, never inside a function, so the tool-call module is one top-level `run(start, 1000)` statement per batch of 1,000 calls (same session, guest loop in the function body).

Secondary measurement, the whole loop as a single top-level statement (no GC until it returns; heap limit raised to 4GiB because garbage accumulates): toolCallWallUs=0.4043, toolCallCpuUs=0.4484 over 1000000 calls.

engines.limitsEnabled: RuntimeLimits: loop_iteration_limit=1000000000, recursion_limit=512, stack_size_limit=10240; no memory limit API; Context::default has no I/O (no boa_runtime)
notes: Session = Context::default() (full realm with intrinsics, default features float16/xsum/temporal) + runtime limits + global call.
Host fn is NativeFunction::from_fn_ptr registered with register_global_callable; reply built with ObjectInitializer and static js_string! keys.

boa_gc collects with stop-the-world mark and sweep: the median batch hides the pauses, so toolCallWallMeanUs and toolCallCpuUs are about twice toolCallWallUs, and the slowest 1,000-call batch averaged 626 us per call (one pause of roughly 0.6 s).

engines.limitsEnabled: ResourceLimits: max_feed_duration=600s, max_turn_duration=10s, max_recursion_depth=1000 (default), max_memory=1GiB with monty-alloc as the global allocator (process-wide accounting), max_suspensions=10000000 enforced by the host loop; no ambient filesystem, env or network
notes: Session = MontyRepl::new with a limited ResourceTracker, then feed_run("1 + 1").

Host calls are suspensions, not callbacks: `call` is an undefined global, so each call pauses the VM with ReplProgress::FunctionCall and the host resumes it with the reply (like the Lua coroutine yield harness); callKind async means suspend/resume.

The argument crosses as a MontyObject graph read through ObjectRef::pairs (allocates a Vec per dict), and the reply is an owned MontyObject dict with three String keys, so every call copies in both directions.

monty's memory limit counts every allocation in the process (monty-alloc is a global counting allocator built for one session per worker process via monty-pool), so in-process it bounds all sessions together; the 1GiB value leaves room for the 1,000-session memory phase.

stabilityCheck.description: the same binary's primary numbers from an earlier full pass on the same host
